concept: Archive loading bay: investigator photographs and measures a cut security seal while the receiving clerk steadies its trolley

new_investigative_sources_exposed.reason: New investigative source A10 requires adult context and two actors with camera/clipboard tools, each with owned hands beyond a marked patch. Frozen input has no declared adult context. The existing second actor steadies a trolley, not a clipboard; no synthetic adult/hand fact is added to admit it. No source use.

composition.chosen: exact independent baseline after three complete alternative comparisons

prospective_gates.evidence: The primary subject holds a camera and a scale against the crate closure while a separate clerk pauses the trolley; evidence marker and controlled loading bay make active investigative documentation readable.

The investigator retains the supplied rounded cheek/face impression, dark eyes, chin-length dark bob and wispy fringe in a clear three-quarter face view. This supports appearance guidance, not real identity.
Her upper right hand visibly owns the compact camera; her arm chain is continuous and the camera points toward the crate-closure work area below it, shared with the scale.
The lower left gloved hand visibly grips the short checker scale and lays its long edge against the crate just below the red seal/hasp area; the glove does not cover the seal.

Red seal pieces and a ragged-looking left end are visible at the hasp, but a matched pair of severed tips with a distinct gap between them cannot be established. The red strip near the hasp may remain connected; a loose/bent strap is a competing reading.
A separate receiving clerk behind the crate has both gloved hands around the same metal trolley handle and looks toward the work area.

A trolley caster and platform corner are visible, but the crate base/platform relation is largely cropped and both actors feet are outside the saved frame. The testcase requires these support endpoints to be assessable together; no bodily defect is diagnosed.
The face, camera grip, scale contact and clerk handle are readable in this frame; the required two cut tips and clear gap remain ambiguous, so the complete gate does not pass.

embodiment_body_ownership.evidence: The primary investigator right arm reaches the compact camera and her left arm reaches the scale. The receiving clerk is a distinct actor whose two gloves remain on the trolley handle. No tool or wrist is transferred between actors.

embodiment_joint_chain_and_reach.evidence: Both investigator shoulder-elbow-wrist paths are readable and reach the separate camera and crate-mounted scale plausibly. The clerk forearms bend toward the shared handle behind the crate without crossing the investigator work zone.

embodiment_support_and_balance.evidence: A caster and a short platform corner are visible, while the crate base and most of the platform are cropped. Both actors lower legs/feet are outside the frame. The complete reviewed support arrangement is not assessable together; this is a visibility limitation, not a diagnosis of implausible hidden anatomy.

embodiment_contact_and_space.evidence: The left glove holds the checker scale flat against the crate below the red closure, with a readable boundary. The camera is separated from the seal and its grip is visible. The clerk gloves contact the metal handle with space between the two work zones.

embodiment_visibility_and_projection.evidence: Face, camera ownership, left-hand scale contact and clerk handle relation are readable together. The planned two severed seal endpoints and clear gap remain ambiguous, and the full support endpoints are cropped, so the entire consequential relation set cannot pass.

user_judgment.evidence: No requesting-user judgment has been received.

pixels.causal_improvement: not established; no before/after image baseline and no newly selected source
